note: MAPPING: codes ARE the S1 workbook's own column names (data/strohacker_2024_situational.py melts the ARMS_* columns unchanged: derivation pattern 1). The names are self-describing abbreviations (PhysFresh, MentalTired, FocusWell, PhysSpent, HandleFeels, CantFocus, UnderControl, FeelFIt, ThinkClear, PhysTired), not item text, so mapping_basis is paper_explicit rather than data_labels: the paper quotes all ten wordings in-text under their five factors (physical readiness 'I feel physically fit'/'I am physically fresh'; physical fatigue 'I am physically tired'/'I am physically spent'; cognitive readiness 'I am thinking clearly'/'I can focus well'; cognitive fatigue 'I cannot focus today'/'I am mentally tired'; threat-challenge readiness 'I have things under control today'/'I can handle unpleasant feelings'), and the workbook's descriptor row names the same pairs (Physical_Readiness = PhysFresh + FeelFit, Physical_Fatigue = PhysSpent + PhysTired, Cognitive_Readiness = FocusWell + ThinkClear, Cognitive_Fatigue = MentalTired + CantFocus, ThreatChallenge_Readiness = HandleFeels + UnderControl). Each name matches exactly one wording, 10/10. TEXT: item_text is the paper's in-text quotation, surrounding quotation marks removed, casing kept, no terminal period added. 'I feel physically fit' is the study's wording (and its code FeelFIt agrees); Keegan et al. 2021's canonical ARMS item PH2 reads 'I am physically fit'. The other nine match Keegan 2021 Table items PH4, PH5R, PH10R, CO2, CO4, CO6R, CO8R, TC13, TC14 verbatim. OPTIONS: 0 'does not apply at all' and 6 'fully applies' from both the paper ('0 = does not apply at all; 6 = fully applies') and the workbook descriptor row ('0=does not apply at all / 1. / 2. / 3. / 4. / 5. / 6=fully applies'); 1-5 are unlabelled in both and left blank. All ten items use all seven levels in the live table. Data are raw (the four fatigue items correlate negatively with all six readiness items), so one anchor set applies to every item. INSTRUCTIONS: left blank. The paper says only that participants gave 'right now' ratings; the administered stem is not published in the paper or any supplement (S1 Checklist docx and S1 Data xlsx checked; s003 and s004 are peer-review/response documents with no ARMS wording; s005 not opened). Keegan 2021's generic ARMS stem was not substituted because this study reframed it. LANGUAGE: pooled English/German administration. The paper: 'Adults in the United States and Germany were recruited' and 'the ARMS, BREQ-3, and PPFS were translated from English to German'. The German wording is in neither the paper nor any supplement, and the workbook carries no cohort flag (ids 1-10, n=8, and 101-123, n=14, plausibly the two sites but not stated). Following the ibrahim_2015_sf36 precedent, language and _translated columns are omitted because English is one of the administered languages; the shipped text is the administered wording for the US cohort only. RIGHTS: ARMS wording originates in Keegan et al. 2021 (Frontiers, CC BY 4.0: 'The use, distribution or reproduction in other forums is permitted, provided the original author(s) and the copyright owner(s) are credited and that the original publication in this journal is cited'). No licence fee, permission requirement, non-commercial, no-derivatives or redistribution clause for the ARMS was located (both Frontiers full texts searched for licence/permission/commercial/copyright terms, finding only the CC BY notice; web search for ARMS permission/licence terms returned only the CC BY article notices). Not in instrument_rights_register.csv. Extracted on silence-is-permission; no register row written (rounds may not write ship rows) -- this is a ship-shaped case for Ben to confirm if a register row is wanted.
